parole.significato: In Egyptian belief, the heart and will and conscience of a person, especially that of the recently deceased which proce…
parole.testo: From the nineteenth-century Lepsius transcription, ȧb, of Egyptian jb (“heart, mind, intention”), ib:Z1.

parole.significato: A kind of quasi-royal priestess in Ancient Egypt.
parole.testo: Calque of Egyptian dwꜣt (“adoratrice”), from dwꜣ (“to worship, to praise”) + -t (feminine ending).

parole.significato: In Egyptian mythology, (roughly) a spirit of the dead that has successfully completed its transition to the afterlife.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian ꜣḫ. Doublet of khu, which derives from an inaccurate older reading of the same word.

parole.significato: The region in the sky in which the sun tarries just before it rises or after it sets.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian ꜣḫt, Ax-x*t:N18.

parole.significato: A cross shaped like a T with a loop at the top, the Egyptian hieroglyph representing the Egyptian triliteral ꜥnḫ (“life…
parole.testo: From Egyptian anx-Z1 (ꜥnḫ, “life, to live, symbol for life”).

parole.significato: A being's soul or personality, represented as a bird-headed figure, which survives after death but must be sustained wi…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian bꜣ, G53-Z1

parole.significato: A sacred stone found in solar temples in ancient Egypt.
parole.testo: From Egyptian bnbn (“Benben, the first mound or stone to arise from the primordial waters at the creation of the world”)—compare bnbnt (“pyramidion”)—and stone.

parole.significato: A measure of weight used during the Middle Kingdom of Ancient Egypt, equivalent to about 13.6 grams.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian dbn.

parole.significato: A red crown of Ancient Egypt symbolizing control over Lower Egypt.
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Egyptian S-r:t*-S3 (dšrt), from S-r-G27 (dšr, “red”) with S3 as determinative + t (-t, feminine ending), thus literally meaning “the red one”.

parole.significato: The realm of the dead in Egyptian mythology.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian dwꜣt.

parole.significato: The sum of bodily parts; the physical body.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian ḥꜥ.

parole.significato: A mystic animating force present in the universe, used by deities and people.
parole.testo: From Egyptian ḥkꜣ.

parole.significato: An Ancient Egyptian dry measure of volume equivalent to 10 hins (or about 4.8 litres).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian ḥqꜣt, H-q:t-:U9.

parole.significato: A subscriber to Afrocentric conspiracy theories.
parole.testo: From Egyptian Htp:t*p (ḥtp, “to be content, at peace; contentment, peace”), a common element of Ancient Egyptian personal names, with the vowels taken over from its descendant, Coptic ϩⲱⲧⲡ̄ (hōtp̄); Ancient Egypt is the focus of several Afrocentric conspiracy theories.

parole.significato: A commercial cultivar of Khorasan wheat.
parole.testo: Taken from kamut, a transcription found in E. A. Wallis Budge's dictionary (where it was translated as "wheat") of Egyptian kꜣmwtt (“ear of barley”), in hieroglyphic form: k-A-m-w-t:t-M2:Z2-

parole.significato: An ancient Egyptian unit of weight, one fiftieth of an avoirdupois pound.
parole.testo: From Egyptian kꜣt.

parole.significato: An Ancient-Egyptian sickle-like sword.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian ḫpš.

parole.significato: Synonym of akh (“a spirit of the dead that has successfully completed its transition to the afterlife”)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian ꜣḫ, following an obsolete 19th-century reading of the word. Doublet of akh, which is based on a more accurate reading.

parole.significato: an honorific phrase used after the names of kings, queens, princes, etc., after the words of a king, ruler, or prince,…
parole.testo: Calque of Egyptian anx-DA-s (ꜥnḫ wḏꜣ snb).

parole.significato: The ancient Egyptian concept of justice, order, and harmony.
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Egyptian mꜣꜥt (“truth, righteousness, justice”).

parole.significato: A kind of short-haired domestic cat.
parole.testo: From mȧu, the rendering of Egyptian mjw (“cat”) in Karl Richard Lepsius’s 19th-century transcription system.

parole.significato: In Ancient Egypt, a heavy beaded necklace and musical instrument with a crescent-shaped plate in the front and a keyhol…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian mnjt in the form of the 19th-century Lepsius-style transcription menȧt.

parole.significato: A pigment made from stibnite and/or galena, once used in Egypt as an eye cosmetic.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian msdmt, where the vowels are uncertain; they are added on the basis of the conventional Egyptological pronunciation. Compare Coptic ⲥⲧⲏⲙ (stēm).

parole.significato: A headcloth worn by pharaohs.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian nms.

parole.significato: One’s name, as part of the soul in ancient Egyptian mythology.
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Egyptian rn, r:n-A2

parole.significato: An Ancient Egyptian board game, probably played as a strategy game similar to chess or go.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian znt — hieroglyphs: z:n-t:N24The full name of the game in Egyptian was znt nt ḥꜥb, which means "game of passing". Compare with Coptic ⲥⲓⲛⲉ (sine, “passing, afternoon”).

parole.significato: In Egyptian hieroglyphs, a rectangular enclosure consisting of a depiction of a palace façade and a top-down view of a…
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Egyptian s-r:x-O33 (srḫ, “palace façade”).

parole.significato: A circle with a line at a tangent to it, represented in hieroglyphs as a stylized loop of rope, representing eternal pr…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian šn (“shen ring, circuit”), a derivative of šnj (“to be round, to encircle”).

parole.significato: a type of loincloth worn in Ancient Egypt
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian šnḏwt.

parole.significato: A Sea Peoples tribe of the late Bronze Age.
parole.testo: From Egyptian šrdn, šꜣrdꜣnꜣ. Possibly cognate to Latin sardus from a pre-Roman substrate language *sard, *shard.

parole.significato: An Ancient Egyptian priest responsible for pouring libations of water.
parole.testo: Calque of Egyptian sqbb (“libator”), participle of sqbb (“to cool, to libate with water”), by way of Ancient Greek σπονδή (spondḗ, “libation”) suffixed with -ist.

parole.significato: An extinct kind of dog from Ancient Egypt resembling a greyhound
parole.testo: From a nineteenth-century transcription of Egyptian ṯzm (“hound”).

parole.significato: A vizier in Ancient Egypt.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian TA-t:Z1-A1 (ṯꜣtj).

parole.significato: An ancient Egyptian symbol of the goddess Isis, resembling an ankh but with the arms curving downward.
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Egyptian tjt.

parole.significato: Synonym of Eye of Horus.
parole.testo: From Egyptian wḏꜣt: w-DA-A-t-wDAt

parole.significato: In Ancient Egypt, a figurine of a dead person, placed in their tomb to do their work for them in the afterlife.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian w-S-b-t:y-A53 (wšbtj, “ushabti”, literally “answerer”), by folk etymology from earlier SA-wA-b-t:y-A53 (šꜣwꜣbtj), perhaps from S-wA-b-M1 (šwꜣb, “persea (tree)”), which may have been the material they were originally made from. The variant forms shawabti, shabti are borrowed di

parole.significato: A type of sceptre with an animal head and a forked tail appearing in Ancient Egyptian art and hieroglyphs.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian wꜣs (“was-sceptre, rule”), compounded with sceptre.

parole.significato: An exclamation of shock.
parole.testo: From Latin Mōsēs, from Ancient Greek Μωσῆς (Mōsês), from earlier Μωυσῆς (Mōusês), from Biblical Hebrew מֹשֶׁה (mōšê). Further etymology is unclear, but it is sometimes conjectured to derive from Egyptian ms-s (msj, “to give birth to”), a common element in Egyptian names of the form ‘[name of deity]

parole.significato: To build up or be arranged in the form of a pyramid.
parole.testo: From French pyramide, from Old French piramide, from Latin pȳramis, pȳramidis, from Ancient Greek πῡραμίς (pūramís), possibly from πῡρός (pūrós, “wheat”) + ἀμάω (amáō, “reap”) or from Egyptian pr-m-ws (“height of a pyramid”), from pr (“(one that) comes forth”) + m (“from”) + ws (“height”). Schenkel

parole.significato: A creature with the head of a person and the body of an animal, commonly a lion.
parole.testo: From Sphinx, from Middle English Spynx, from Latin Sphinx, from Ancient Greek Σφίγξ (Sphínx), perhaps either from σφίγγω (sphíngō, “to squeeze, to strangle”) (whence also sphincter), of Pre-Greek origin, or from Egyptian Szp:p-A53-anx-n:x (šzp-ꜥnḫ, “divine image”, literally “living image”).

parole.significato: An evaporite, consisting of mixture of sodium carbonate and sodium bicarbonate, Na₃HCO₃CO₃·2H₂O.
parole.testo: From Swedish trona or from Spanish trona, both derived from Arabic أَطْرُون (ʔaṭrūn), from نَطْرُون (naṭrūn), from Ancient Greek νίτρον (nítron), ultimately from Egyptian nṯrj: R9. Doublet of natron and niter.
